results.name: Five specific modules extend all 188 existing parts to 193 unique identities
Module starters have editable embedded source, unassigned pins and no default mounting drills
BME original header preserves 2.54 mm pitch and regulator output identity
Original DS3231 has all eight named contacts including battery, 32 kHz, SQW and RESET
OLED display-face reflection retains pin identities, VIN7 and GND8
TB6612 keeps motor and logic input apart and labels all sixteen contacts
MPM3610 3.3 V header preserves source R180 order: EN,VIN,OUT,GND
Optional module mounting holes follow rotation and bottom-side transforms
Showing or hiding module bodies is neutral to manufacturing output
Module bodies and editor captions produce no silkscreen without explicit ref enable
Conflicting nets on module internally common GND contacts are errors
Nominal underside interference remains advisory and source-review flag is explicit
Malformed module sources, flags and non-finite dimensions are rejected
Unknown user module identity remains losslessly editable without registry lookup
Module pin CSV applies spreadsheet-escape protection
Six built-in blocks are valid self-contained schema-1 templates
All six saved-copper starters have no unrouted connection or copper errors
Each insertion allocates fresh refs and retains source footprint identity
Repeated blocks have disjoint net and object identities, including RETURN/GND
Explicit port mapping shares only that selected existing net
Non-port mapping, missing target and accidental port short are atomic failures
Every template supports moving, rotating and flipping complete copper coherently
Transforming forward and backward preserves part/pad/trace/via geometry
Locked block members reject a group transform without partial mutation
Individual edits remain normal objects, not library-linked replacements
Copying a modified block preserves edits, removes double-scoping and allocates fresh nets
Project JSON round-trip preserves block instances and personal templates
Capturing a selection without copper preserves net intent but is unrouted on insertion
Capturing standalone silk/holes/zones is rejected instead of silently dropping them
Attaching mounting-hole and RF keepout metadata survives block capture and insertion
Block export captures actual current geometry, not the original library seed
Document imports reject orphan, repeated or double-owned block members
Deleting a member prunes the group; deleting all members removes the empty record
Detaching a block never changes parts, copper, nets or manufacturing output
Schema 1/2/3/4 migration adds empty block containers without changing geometry
Unsupported project and block schemas fail rather than lose metadata
Malformed, oversized or empty block payloads are rejected
Duplicate personal library IDs and built-in ID overrides are rejected
Placement preflight rejects new shorts against existing differently assigned copper
Placement preflight rejects outside-board copper with no destination mutation
Preflight permits unrouted intent and remote explicit port mapping without ignoring physical shorts
Review findings distinguish topology examples from verified electrical operation
Explicit whole-net merge updates group port records and remains exportable
Explicit merging of two former ports exports one combined net rather than corrupting a block
KiCad output retains ordinary copper/net geometry while omitting group metadata
Module ground lead can connect to an assigned bottom plane through its plated pad
Both samplers validate and contain no initial copper error
